groups.name: Trinucleotide repeat expansion disorders
groups.explanation: All four are caused by a DNA repeat of three letters that grows longer each generation, so symptoms start earlier and get worse in children (anticipation).

article.text: HTT gene, chromosome 4: Huntington disease. A CAG repeat in huntingtin kills neurons in the caudate, causing chorea.
CGG: Fragile X syndrome. This repeat silences the FMR1 gene.
Can't let go after a handshake: Myotonic dystrophy. A CTG repeat stops muscles relaxing after they contract.
Staggering gait with pes cavus: Friedreich ataxia. A GAA repeat causes ataxia and a thickened heart.

groups.name: Defects of collagen synthesis
groups.explanation: All four break a different step of building collagen, so skin, bone, vessels, and gums lose their strength.

article.text: Swollen, bleeding gums: Scurvy. No vitamin C, so proline and lysine are not hydroxylated.
Blue sclerae: Osteogenesis imperfecta. Bad type I collagen chains cannot form the triple helix.
Hyperextensible skin: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Faulty collagen processing and cross-linking make skin and joints too loose.
Kinky, brittle hair in an infant boy: Menkes disease. No copper for lysyl oxidase, so fibers never cross-link.
Images: scorbutic gums, CDC (public domain); blue sclerae, Herbert L. Fred, MD and Hendrik A. van Dijk (CC BY-SA 3.0); stretched skin, Rollcloud (CC0). All via Wikimedia Commons.

groups.name: Agents that cut the signal from nerve to muscle
groups.explanation: Each one stops the message from nerve to muscle. Two block the nerve's Na+ channels, one stops ACh release, and one jams the muscle's ACh receptor.

article.text: Pufferfish: Tetrodotoxin. Blocks Na+ channels, so the nerve cannot fire.
Lidocaine: Local anesthetic. Blocks the same Na+ channels. (It is also a Cardio antiarrhythmic, the decoy.)
Bulging can: Botulinum toxin. Cuts SNARE proteins, so ACh is never released.
Succinylcholine: Depolarizing blocker. Keeps the muscle ACh receptor switched on until it stops responding.
Images: pufferfish, Dotun55 (CC BY-SA 4.0); bulging can, Kat1100 (CC BY 4.0); succinylcholine vial, Mark Oniffrey (CC BY-SA 4.0). All via Wikimedia Commons.

groups.name: Clues that point to asthma
groups.explanation: One disease seen four ways: a drug that sets it off, the test that proves it, and two things found in the sputum.

article.text: Propranolol: A nonselective beta-blocker. It blocks the beta-2 receptors that keep airways open, so it can set off an attack.
Methacholine: The challenge test. Inhaling it tightens twitchy asthmatic airways when spirometry looks normal.
Sputum smear: Curschmann spirals, coiled mucus casts of the small airways.
Sputum, high power: Charcot-Leyden crystals, needle-shaped crystals left behind by eosinophils.

Images: propranolol boxes, Whispyhistory (CC BY-SA 4.0); Curschmann spirals, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by a working pathologist (Attribution license); Charcot-Leyden crystals, Atlas of Medical Foreign Bodies (CC BY-SA 2.0), via Wikimedia Commons.

info.title: Huntington disease
info.text: Gene clue: the huntingtin gene on chromosome 4. Expanded CAG repeats kill neurons in the caudate, causing chorea in middle age.

info.title: Fragile X syndrome
info.text: Sequence clue: a CGG repeat that silences the FMR1 gene, causing a long face, large ears, and macroorchidism.

items.label: Can't let go after a handshake

info.title: Myotonic dystrophy
info.text: Exam clue: the muscle can't relax after a single contraction, with cataracts, frontal balding, and gonadal atrophy. The repeat is CTG.

info.title: Friedreich ataxia
info.text: Exam clue: a child with ataxia, kyphoscoliosis, pes cavus, diabetes, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The repeat is GAA.

info.title: Scurvy
info.text: Exam clue: swollen gums, easy bruising, and hemarthrosis in someone living on tea and toast. Vitamin C is missing for proline and lysine hydroxylation.

info.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta
info.text: Exam clue: blue sclerae and fractures after minimal trauma. A COL1A1 or COL1A2 defect ruins the type I collagen triple helix.

info.title: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
info.text: Exam clue: skin that stretches far past normal, hypermobile joints, and easy bruising from faulty collagen synthesis.

items.label: Kinky, brittle hair in an infant boy

info.title: Menkes disease
info.text: Exam clue: an X-linked ATP7A defect blocks copper transport, so lysyl oxidase can't cross-link collagen. The hair is brittle and kinky.

info.title: Tetrodotoxin
info.text: Dinner clue: a diner has tingling lips, then weakness, after a fugu meal. The pufferfish toxin plugs fast Na+ channels so the axon can't fire.

info.title: Lidocaine
info.text: Rx clue: an amide injected before stitching a laceration. It blocks Na+ channels from the inside so the nerve goes quiet.

info.title: Botulinum toxin
info.text: Pantry clue: descending flaccid paralysis starting with the eyes. The toxin cleaves SNARE proteins so ACh is never released.

info.title: Succinylcholine
info.text: Rx clue: given for rapid intubation. It binds the nicotinic ACh receptor and keeps the end plate depolarized, so the muscle can't contract again.

info.title: Propranolol
info.text: Rx clue: a nonselective beta-blocker. It blocks beta-2 receptors on airway smooth muscle, so it's avoided in this disease.

info.title: Methacholine
info.text: PFT clue: inhaled during a challenge test when the disease is suspected but spirometry comes back normal.

info.title: Curschmann spirals
info.text: Sputum clue: coiled, spiral-shaped mucus plugs shed from the small airways.

info.title: Charcot-Leyden crystals
info.text: Sputum clue: thin, needle-shaped crystals made from eosinophil protein.
